glossary_terms.definition: The legal form a business takes, such as sole trader, partnership, private limited company or public limited company.
A business owned and run by one person who keeps all the profit and has unlimited liability.
The owner of a business is personally responsible for all the business's debts — their own assets can be taken to pay them.
A business owned by 2–20 partners who share responsibility, profit and unlimited liability.
A company whose shares are sold privately — usually to family, friends or invited investors — and are not traded on the stock exchange.
Shareholders can only lose the amount they invested in the company — their personal assets are protected.
A company whose shares are traded on the stock exchange and can be bought by any member of the public.
An organisation that trades with a social aim — any surplus is reinvested rather than paid to owners.
